sections.h2: What sets a Winslow sale apart from other Camden County sales?
sections.html:
A Winslow closing depends on two separate approvals: a township resale certificate from the Construction Official and an alarm certificate from the Winslow Township Fire District. The township is also the biggest in Camden County by area, and much of its land lies in the Pinelands.

Below you will find market figures, both inspections with their fees, the Camden County filing and the township's tax rules, ending with a plain comparison of an agent listing, a sale by yourself and an as-is cash buyer.

sections.h2: What do the Winslow figures show about homes and incomes?
sections.html:
The 2020 census put Winslow at 39,907 people, and the mid-2025 estimate is 40,562. Those residents are spread across 57.42 square miles of land, only 695 per square mile, which fits the pine woods and farm parcels between its villages.

sections.h2: What shaped Winslow's neighborhoods and the Pinelands around them?
sections.html:
Winslow was incorporated on March 8, 1845 from part of Gloucester Township, and its early economy ran on glass works that drew on local timber, clay and sand. By the 1970 census it still had only 11,202 residents.

Growth followed the Atlantic City Expressway interchange at Williamstown Road, finished in 1965. Levitt and Sons then built thousands of homes in the Sicklerville section, and the population reached 20,034 in 1980 and 30,087 in 1990. Today the township includes unincorporated communities such as Sicklerville, Cedar Brook, Blue Anchor, Tansboro, Braddock, Albion and Williamstown.

Much of the land is protected: Wikipedia reports that around 80 percent of the township sat inside the Pinelands National Reserve in 2006. The New Jersey Pinelands span 1.1 million acres, and the Pinelands Commission can be reached at (609) 894-7300. For a large lot, or a buyer who plans a new structure, ask the Commission which approvals apply before you promise anything.

sections.h2: How do the Expressway, the buses and the schools affect Winslow buyers?
sections.html:
Roads total 245.16 miles, divided among the township, Camden County, the state and the South Jersey Transportation Authority. The Atlantic City Expressway cuts through the southwest with Exits 31, 33, 38 and 41, and Route 73, Route 143 and U.S. Route 30 also run through town.

Transit means buses. NJ Transit's 400 route links Sicklerville with Philadelphia, and the Avandale park-and-ride has 322 parking spaces. Wikipedia notes that no bus stops within reasonable walking distance of the municipal building, so most households drive.

Winslow Township School District had eight schools and 5,024 students in 2023-24, with four elementary schools through grade 3, two upper elementary schools for grades 4 to 6, one middle school and Winslow Township High School. The district formed in 1998 after voters approved a split from the Lower Camden County Regional district, and it also teaches students from Chesilhurst.

sections.h2: What does the Winslow resale certificate involve?
sections.html:
Under Chapter 205 of the township code, retitled Resale Certificates by a February 2025 ordinance, every existing dwelling needs a certificate of continued occupancy before occupancy changes. Applicants go to the Township Construction Official, who inspects for habitability and compliance with the code.

  • Residential applications cost $100.
  • Payment by check triggers a 10 working-day wait before the inspection.
  • The Construction Official has 10 working days from a complete application and fee to inspect and then issue the certificate or list the violations.
  • The first reinspection is free, and each later one costs $50.
  • No one may occupy the dwelling until life-hazard violations are corrected.
  • Violating the chapter carries a penalty from $250 up to $1,000.

The ordinance has an unusual option. A buyer can assume the seller's duty through a written waiver acknowledging responsibility for the certificate, and the waiver is filed with the Construction Official.

sections.h2: What happens at the Winslow fire inspection?
sections.html:
State law calls for an alarm inspection before a home is sold, and the Winslow Fire Prevention Division performs it. A firefighter sprays test smoke into each smoke alarm, presses the carbon monoxide test button and checks for a secondary power source label. A passing house earns a certificate to carry to settlement.

  • The fee is $65 with eight or more days of notice, $100 with four to seven days and $150 with three days or fewer.
  • A senior aged 62 or older with proof of age pays $30.
  • Reinspections and missed appointments cost $35 each.
  • Alarms past ten years of age must go, and the manufacture date is printed on the underside of each device.
  • Solar panels, a generator or battery storage call for a permanent printed label at the panel and meter warning of multiple sources of power.
  • The fire district will not go in on a lockbox, and its office says it answers online applications within 24 hours.

An all-electric house with no fireplace or attached garage needs only smoke alarms. Questions about your layout go to the Fire Marshal at 609-561-4225.

sections.h2: Which county office records a Winslow deed, and how do local taxes work?
sections.html:
Camden County's Clerk records Winslow deeds from Room 102 at 520 Market Street in Camden, phone (856) 225-5300. The clerk's page advertises electronic recording and appointment booking, so a title company can usually file on your behalf.

Installments come due on the first of February, May, August and November. A ten-day courtesy period follows, but the collector must physically hold the payment by the end of the tenth day, since postmarks do not count. Delinquent amounts up to $1,500 carry 8 percent interest and larger ones carry 18 percent, and a balance above $10,000 at year end adds a 6 percent penalty. Anything left in the township drop box counts as received the next business day.

Added and omitted assessment bills go out in October and fall due November 1. The 2026 tax sale was scheduled for October 8, and the township points out that taxes and utility charges attach to the property itself. Request a payoff figure from the tax office before closing.

sections.h2: Is an agent, a solo sale or a cash buyer right for a Winslow house?
sections.html:
An agent listing usually reaches the widest pool of buyers, a cash buyer sidesteps the repair cycle, and a solo sale saves commission for owners who can manage the paperwork. The house's condition and your deadline settle the question.

  • Use an agent if the house is in good order and you can wait while a mortgage buyer passes the township inspection.
  • Go solo if you will manage showings, the contract and both Winslow inspections.
  • Choose an as-is cash buyer if repairs, tenants or an estate would slow a conventional sale, because that buyer can sign the resale waiver and take over any violations.

Whatever you pick, request a Fire District date as soon as a closing is set, and file the township application early enough to give the inspector the 10 working days the ordinance allows.

faqs.q: How much is the Winslow resale certificate?
faqs.a: The township charges $100 for a residential dwelling. The first reinspection is free and later ones cost $50. The separate fire inspection runs $65 to $150 depending on notice, with a $30 senior rate.

faqs.q: Who must obtain the Winslow certificate, seller or buyer?
faqs.a: The seller by default, though a buyer may assume the duty through a written waiver filed with the Construction Official. The waiver must say the buyer knows the responsibility is being taken over.

faqs.q: How fast can a Winslow fire inspection be arranged?
faqs.a: The fire district says it replies within a day of an online application, and fees rise with less than eight days of notice. Bring the certificate to settlement.

faqs.q: What are the Winslow tax installment dates?
faqs.a: The first of February, May, August and November, followed by ten grace days. Postmarks are not honored, and late interest runs back to the original due date.

faqs.q: Where do Winslow house deeds get filed?
faqs.a: With the Camden County Clerk, Room 102 at 520 Market Street, Camden. The phone number is (856) 225-5300.
